title: Derived adic completeness
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and let
$\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be
the integral and finite coefficient sheaves of
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A complex
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ is *derived complete* if its canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. For
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the canonical
transitions satisfy the derived reduction identities
$K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K_n$;
a compatible tower with these identities is called *normalized*.

Normalization is a property of the complexes $K_n$; their cohomology sheaves
$H^q(K_n)$ need not form a normalized tower under the ordinary tensor product.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, $n\ge1$. The coefficient constructions give $R\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Use the unbounded Layer B category $D(\Mod_R)$ and its relative derived tensor.

The canonical mapModComapIso identifies the pulled-back coefficient module with the restricted regular quotient module; its underlying identity makes the unit and transition hypotheses exactly the specified coefficient maps. The resulting level isomorphisms identify termwise tensor reductions and their units and transitions with integralLevel and integralStep, with no flat-term or section-module comparison.

proof.text: Pro-etale repleteness gives the epimorphism of the zero projection of a countable inverse sequence in abelian sheaves. Mod.epiπAppZeroOfEpi lifts this to native internal modules, and CountableAB4Star.of_epi_π_app_zero gives exact countable products. Apply lem-weil-derived-countable-products-core to the termwise tower. Construct the signed coordinate isomorphism from mappingCocone(1-s) to the explicit roos complex, sending its second coordinate to its negative; verify its differential and inverse directly. Transport the distinguished cocone triangle through localization and the unique product comparison. Projecting its first map onto each factor and using the scalar-unit identities proves the displayed completionMap equation.

proof.text: For representative independence refine a derived isomorphism to a common right-fraction roof and replace its vertex by a native K-flat resolution (the generic exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat source theorem attached to lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution). Tensoring a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes with any fixed coefficient preserves quasi-isomorphisms by acyclicity of its K-flat cone. Exact countable products preserve their levelwise quasi-isomorphisms. The explicit diagonal coordinate map of the two Roos models is a quasi-isomorphism by lem-pe-roos-coordinates-quasi-iso and commutes with the (unit,0) augmentations. Cancel the two localized roof legs; then cancel the representative isomorphism in completionMap. This proves isDerivedComplete_iff.

proof.text: The reduction comparison is defined by left-adjoint uniqueness for the composite extension-restriction adjunction. The mate of the specified transition is its isomorphism by the triangle identities, proving derivedReduction_isNormalized. The same uniqueness identity identifies the composite of the two actual units with the direct unit, proving reductionUnit_compatible. No additional successive-quotient comparison theorem is used.

proof.text: For the warning take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and $K=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. By [lem-pe-two-term-reduction-cohomology] its ordinary cohomology reduction comparison in degree $-1$ is zero between nonzero copies of $k_X$. It cannot be invertible: an inverse would imply $1_{k_X}=0$. Its complex reduction tower is normalized by step 4, giving the required distinction.

blueprint_update.statement:
We treat integral coefficients through their reductions modulo powers of $\pi_E$. This is
possible for complexes that are recovered from their reductions, the derived complete ones.
Derived completeness is the analogue for complexes of the condition
$M=\varprojlim_nM/\pi_E^nM$ on a module. For example, $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ itself is derived
complete, while $E_X$ is not, since all its reductions vanish.

Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and let
$\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be
the integral and finite coefficient sheaves of
[det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A complex
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ is *derived complete* if its canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. For
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the canonical
transitions satisfy the derived reduction identities
$K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K_n$;
a compatible tower with these identities is called *normalized*.

Normalization is a property of the complexes $K_n$. Their cohomology sheaves
$H^q(K_n)$ in general do not form a normalized tower under the ordinary
tensor product.
